name: MonarchAiMemoryChip
title: AiMemoryChip
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.AssistChip with androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu and androidx.compose.material3.AlertDialog; the row variant and the read-only chip are a Row with the Monarch surface
summary: One thing the assistant remembers, from a MonarchAiMemoryPart, shown as "Remembered: …" with a menu to edit or forget it.
whenToUse: Inside an assistant reply, to show a memory the assistant used, saved or forgot, and in a list of memories (the Row variant) where people review and correct what the assistant keeps.
whenNotToUse: For what the next prompt will see use MonarchAiContextChips. For a plain label on data use MonarchTag.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiMemoryChip(memory: MonarchAiMemoryPart, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant = MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant.Chip, showScope: Boolean? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels = MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels(), onEdit: ((id: String, text: String) -> Unit)? = null, onForget: ((id: String) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

class MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels(prefix: ((action: MonarchAiMemoryAction) -> String)? = null, options: String? = null, edit: String? = null, forget: String? = null, editTitle: String? = null, editField: String? = null, save: String? = null, cancel: String? = null)

options.name: memory
options.description: The memory from the conversation model: its id, action (Read, Write, Forget), text and scope.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the chip or the row.

options.name: variant
options.description: Chip: an inline pill in the AI colors with the prefix. Row: a full-width row without the prefix.

options.name: showScope
options.description: Whether the scope is shown under the text. By default on the chip and not on the row.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph at the start, tinted with the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the prefixes, the tap action name, Edit, Forget and the edit dialog strings.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Adds Edit. Receives the id and the trimmed new text; never called with empty or unchanged text.

options.name: onForget
options.description: Adds Forget. Runs at once, without confirmation.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the press, focus and hover interactions of the chip or the row.

states.name: forget
states.description: Prefix "Forgotten:" (also on the row), muted struck-through text and no commands.

states.name: read only
states.description: No callbacks: text only, not a button.

states.name: editable
states.description: Tapping opens a menu with Edit and Forget, as given; TalkBack offers both as actions.

states.name: editing
states.description: A dialog with a text field, Save and Cancel. Save is disabled while the text is empty or unchanged.

appearance: The chip is a pill with the AI subtle fill, the AI border and default text with a bold prefix; the icon uses the AI strong color. The row uses the surface fill and the subtle border. A forgotten memory uses the muted fill, muted text and the subtle border, with the text struck through. The menu uses the raised background; Forget is in the danger strong color.
platformNotes: Built on the shared MonarchAiMemoryPart, as on iOS: the web's entity becomes the part's scope and the prefix follows the part's action (the web always says "Remembered:"). The parity map names InputChip, but an InputChip is a selectable chip that TalkBack reads as checked or not checked; the chip opens a menu, so it is an AssistChip, which has the button role. The web's separate Edit and Forget buttons and the iOS menu button are a DropdownMenu opened by tapping the chip itself, because Monarch for Android bundles no menu glyph; both are also TalkBack custom actions. Editing happens in an AlertDialog with a multi-line field instead of inline, so there are no Enter and Escape shortcuts. The row shows "Forgotten:" for a forgotten memory so its state never depends on the strike-through. The web's leading and meta slots are not offered. Same names as iOS; iOS's options closure (a spoken name built from the text) is a plain tap action name here, because the chip's own text is its name.
accessibility: The prefix, the text and the scope are one TalkBack element.
An editable chip has the button role and a 48dp touch target; an editable row is a button at least 48dp high whose tap action is read as "show options".
Edit and Forget are TalkBack custom actions of the element as well as menu items.
A forgotten memory is struck through and also says "Forgotten:", so the state does not depend on the line.
The icon slot is decoration; the prefix says that the assistant kept the memory.
The edit field is labelled "Memory" and Save reports itself disabled while it cannot save.
edgeCases: Long text wraps; the chip grows in height.
An empty or white-space scope is never shown.
A forgotten memory offers no commands even when callbacks are given.
Saving text that only differs by spaces at the ends is treated as unchanged.

examples.title: Read only
The memories of a message, read only
examples.code:
val message = MonarchAiConversationMessage(
    id = "a1",
    role = MonarchAiRole.Assistant,
    parts = listOf(MonarchAiMemoryPart(id = "m2", action = MonarchAiMemoryAction.Read, text = "Works in Lisbon")),
    createdAt = "2025-03-10T12:00:00.000Z",
)
message.memories.forEach { memory -> MonarchAiMemoryChip(memory = memory) }

examples.title: A row in a list of memories
examples.code:
MonarchAiMemoryChip(
    memory = MonarchAiMemoryPart(id = "m3", action = MonarchAiMemoryAction.Write, text = "Team: Payments"),
    variant = MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant.Row,
    onEdit = { _, _ -> },
    onForget = {},
)
